promptLatex: A game costs 2 dollars to play. A fair six-sided die is rolled, and a 6 pays 12 dollars while any other result pays nothing. What is the expected net gain or loss from playing the game once?
hintLatex: A win has net value $12 - 2 = 10$ and a loss has net value $-2$.
The win has probability $\frac{1}{6}$ and the loss has probability $\frac{5}{6}$.
solutionLatex:
Playing costs $2$ in every case. Rolling a 6 gives a net of $12 - 2 = 10$, with probability $\frac{1}{6}$, and any other result gives a net of $-2$, with probability $\frac{5}{6}$.

E[\text{net}] = \frac{1}{6} \cdot 10 + \frac{5}{6} \cdot (-2) = \frac{10 - 10}{6} = 0.

The game is fair: over many plays the winnings exactly repay the stake. Every individual play loses money, which is why the mean and not the typical outcome is the right thing to examine.
